title: Conditional machine computes exactly the selected branch
statement: Let $D,M_1,M_2$ be finite Turing machines over the Boolean alphabet, and let $p:\{0,1\}^*\to\{0,1\}$ be a Boolean-valued function. Suppose that for every input $y$, $D$ computes the singleton output $[p(y)]$ within some finite number of steps. For every Boolean word $x$ and output word $w$, the conditional machine built from $D,M_1,M_2$ computes $w$ from $x$ within some finite number of steps if and only if the machine selected by the bit $p(x)$ computes $w$ from $x$ within some finite number of steps.
